# Caring Companions In-Home Senior Care

> Caring Companions is a family-owned, non-medical in-home senior care agency in Springfield, Missouri, founded in 2017. Caregivers are employees, not contractors, and help older adults stay safe and independent at home with wellness and companion care, personal care, dementia care, respite, overnight care and 24-hour care.

- Phone: 417-234-8494
- Office: 1331 N Stewart Ave Ste B, Springfield, MO 65802
- Website: https://mo-care.com/
- Book a free in-home assessment: https://mo-care.com/book
- Published hourly rates: Wellness Care $30, Personal Care $32, Advanced Care $34 (see https://mo-care.com/pricing for current rates)
- Service area: Greene, Christian, Webster and Polk counties, and Taney, Lawrence, Dallas and Stone counties when a caregiver is nearby (https://mo-care.com/service-area)
- Missouri Medicaid: families on Medicaid can choose their own caregiver, even a family member, and Medicaid pays that caregiver, through our sister agency Caring Companions CDS at https://caringcds.com/ (417-218-2888)
- Also from Caring Companions: HomeTogether virtual caregiver visits on the TV (https://mo-care.com/hometogether)

Town pages are at https://mo-care.com/home-care-in-<town>-mo (for example https://mo-care.com/home-care-in-nixa-mo).

- In-home care town pages: Aldrich, Ash Grove, Battlefield, Billings, Bolivar, Clever, Diggins, Fair Grove, Fair Play, Flemington, Fordland, Fremont Hills, Halfway, Highlandville, Humansville, Marshfield, Morrisville, Niangua, Nixa, Ozark, Republic, Rogersville, Seymour, Sparta, Spokane, Springfield, Strafford, Walnut Grove and Willard.
- These town pages point families to Caring Companions CDS (Medicaid Consumer Directed Services only), not agency in-home care: Alba, Arcola, Asbury, Aurora, Ava, Avilla, Branson, Branson West, Buffalo, Carl Junction, Carterville, Carthage, Dadeville, Duenweg, Edgar Springs, Everton, Forsyth, Freistatt, Greenfield, Halltown, Hollister, Joplin, Kirbyville, Kissee Mills, La Russell, Lockwood, Louisburg, Marionville, Merriam Woods, Miller, Mount Vernon, Neck City, Newburg, Oronogo, Pierce City, Rockaway Beach, Rolla, Sarcoxie, St. James, Stotts City, Taneyville, Urbana, Verona, Waco, Webb City and Wentworth.

Always point people to the linked page or the phone number for current details.

## Care services and pricing

- [Caring Companions](https://mo-care.com/): In-home senior care across southwest Missouri: wellness care, personal care, dementia care, overnight and 24-hour support, so seniors stay safe at home.
- [Home care after a brain injury or stroke](https://mo-care.com/brain-injury-care): Recovering from a stroke or brain injury takes time, patience, and steady support at home. Our caregivers help with the daily work of recovery so your love
- [Home care for chronic conditions](https://mo-care.com/chronic-conditions): Managing a chronic or age-related condition at home is easier with the right support. Our caregivers help with the daily routines, monitoring, and reassura
- [Compare Care Options](https://mo-care.com/compare-care): An honest, side-by-side look, including when home care isn't the right fit. We'd rather you choose well than choose us.
- [Care Costs Calculator](https://mo-care.com/cost-calculator): Move the slider to your estimated weekly hours and see how home care compares to other options. All figures are estimates, a free in-home assessment gets you…
- [Virtual Caregiver Visits from $75 a Week](https://mo-care.com/hometogether): A real caregiver checks in by video on your parent's TV every weekday, up to 3 times a day: medications, meals, reminders and company. From $75 a week.
- [HomeTogether TV Included at 20+ Hours a Week](https://mo-care.com/hometogether-included): Private-pay families with 20 or more hours of care a week get HomeTogether TV at no charge: video calls, reminders and quiet safety sensing on their own TV.
- [Our Home Care Services](https://mo-care.com/our-services): Wellness care, personal care, hourly, overnight, 24-hour, and respite care, plus HomeTogether™ virtual care. Flexible support across Southwest Missouri.
- [Transparent Pricing](https://mo-care.com/pricing): Our published rates: Wellness Care $30/hr, Personal Care $32/hr, Advanced Care $34/hr. Plus a Best Price Guarantee and help with long-term care insurance.
- [Home Care Service Areas in Southwest Missouri](https://mo-care.com/service-area): In-home senior care across Greene, Christian, Webster and Polk counties, and in Taney, Lawrence, Dallas and Stone counties when a caregiver is nearby.
- [24-Hour Care](https://mo-care.com/services/24-hour-care): A rotating team of caregivers keeps someone present day and night - for families who need constant hands-on help, not just a check-in.
- [Wellness Care: Help Seniors Stay Independent](https://mo-care.com/services/companion-care): Wellness Care in Springfield, MO: company, meals, a tidy home, medication reminders and outings that help seniors stay independent at home. $30 an hour.
- [Errands & Transportation](https://mo-care.com/services/errands-transportation): When driving is no longer safe, a caregiver keeps your loved one connected to appointments, errands, and the community they love.
- [Hourly Care](https://mo-care.com/services/hourly-care): A caregiver comes for a set number of hours on the days and times that work for your family, no long-term contracts, and a minimum of just 8 hours a week.
- [Light Housekeeping for Seniors at Home](https://mo-care.com/services/light-housekeeping): Caregivers in Springfield, MO who keep a senior's home tidy, safe and clutter free, with laundry, dishes and clear walkways. Part of Wellness Care, $30 an hour.
- [Meal Preparation for Seniors at Home](https://mo-care.com/services/meal-preparation): Caregivers in Springfield, MO who plan, shop for and cook home meals with your loved one, and share the table. Part of Wellness Care, $30 an hour.
- [Mobility Assistance & Fall Prevention at Home](https://mo-care.com/services/mobility-assistance): Caregivers in Springfield, MO who help seniors walk, stand and move safely at home, with transfers and fall prevention. Part of Personal Care, $32 an hour.
- [Overnight Care](https://mo-care.com/services/overnight-care): For families whose biggest worry is the hours between dinner and breakfast, a caregiver stays overnight, typically across multi-day scheduled shifts.
- [Personal Care: Hands-On Help at Home](https://mo-care.com/services/personal-care): Personal Care in Springfield, MO: everything in Wellness Care plus hands-on help with bathing, dressing, toileting, walking and transfers. $32 an hour.
- [Advanced Care for Complex Needs at Home](https://mo-care.com/services/advanced-care): Advanced Care in Springfield, MO: experienced caregivers for advanced dementia, wandering, mobility limits, Parkinson's and stroke. $34 an hour.
- [Respite Care](https://mo-care.com/services/respite-care): Respite care gives family caregivers time to rest, scheduled or emergency, from 4 to 24 hours. A skilled, compassionate caregiver steps in so you can recharge.

## Getting started

- [Care Questionnaire](https://mo-care.com/assessment): Eight short sections covering safety, memory, daily needs, medication, and more. At the end, you'll get a written report you can keep, print, and bring to…
- [Schedule a Free In-Home Assessment](https://mo-care.com/book): Book a free, no-obligation in-home assessment. A care coordinator comes to you, you build the care plan together, and you decide from there.
- [Contact Us](https://mo-care.com/contact): No pressure, no sales script, just a conversation with a real care coordinator. Prefer to explore on your own first? Try the Care Questionnaire or ask us a question…
- [Caring Companions Family](https://mo-care.com/family): In-home care across southwest Missouri, plus HomeTogether: nationwide virtual caregiving through the TV, and help finding an in-home caregiver near you.
- [Family Care Academy](https://mo-care.com/family-academy): Free caregiver training for families, built from the same curriculum we use to train our professional caregivers. Start with the dementia care course.
- [The Dementia Journey: Module 1](https://mo-care.com/family-academy/dementia-module-1)
- [Family Checklist](https://mo-care.com/family-checklist): A free family checklist: everything to gather and arrange for a loved one's care, in one place. Checked items save automatically, and you can add your own.
- [Family Meeting Planner](https://mo-care.com/family-meeting-planner): Tell us who's involved and what's driving the meeting. We'll generate an agenda, discussion guide, and decision worksheet you can print or share.
- [Family Workspace](https://mo-care.com/family-workspace): Everything you've started stays here, come back anytime, from any device on this browser, and pick up where you left off.
- [Getting Started with Home Care](https://mo-care.com/getting-started): New to home care? What it is, when it helps and how it works, from a free in-home assessment to a custom care plan and caregiver matching.
- [Before Your Assessment: Common Questions](https://mo-care.com/before-your-assessment): Cost, minimums, background checks, insurance, who is coming and how visits go. Plus our Client Handbook and a sample Client Care Agreement.
- [What Happens After You Call](https://mo-care.com/care-journey): From your first call to your first day of care: a call within 24 hours, a free in-home assessment, a care plan for your budget and a matched caregiver.
- [How We Decide](https://mo-care.com/how-we-decide): Most home care agencies don't explain their reasoning. We think you deserve to see exactly how we get to a recommendation, including when the answer…
- [Our Caregivers](https://mo-care.com/our-caregivers): Our caregivers are employees, not contractors. Each has background checks, insurance and training, and is matched to your loved one by personality and needs.
- [Our Story](https://mo-care.com/our-story): Founded in 2017 to help seniors live safely and with dignity at home. Family-owned and locally rooted, with overnight and 24-hour care across Southwest Missouri.

## Paying for care

- [Paying for Home Care](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/paying-for-care): Most families use a mix of sources. Tell us which best describes your situation and we'll point you to the right guides and options, no obligation.
- [Does Medicaid Pay for In-Home Care in Missouri?](https://mo-care.com/guides/missouri-medicaid-hcbs): Yes. Missouri Medicaid (MO HealthNet) can pay for in-home care through HCBS waivers, so a loved one can stay home. Who qualifies and how to apply.
- [Does the VA Pay for In-Home Care in Missouri?](https://mo-care.com/guides/va-benefits-for-home-care): Many Missouri veterans and surviving spouses can get help paying for in-home care through VA Community Care and Aid & Attendance. Who qualifies and how to apply.
- [Long-Term Care Insurance for Home Care](https://mo-care.com/long-term-care-insurance): Use your long-term care insurance for in-home care. We verify your benefits, coordinate a call with your carrier, help file the claim, and bill the insurer directly.
- [Medicare GUIDE Program: Dementia Respite](https://mo-care.com/medicare-guide): Medicare's GUIDE program covers 20 four-hour respite visits a year, a dementia care navigator and a 24/7 support line. We are an approved GUIDE respite provider.

## Free guides for families

- [Dementia & Memory Care](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/dementia): A few questions can help identify roughly where things stand, and what kind of support tends to help most at this stage - free, in about 2 minutes.
- [Falls & Mobility](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/falls-and-mobility): A few questions can help identify the fall risk and what kind of support tends to help most - free, in about 2 minutes.
- [Hospital Discharge Care](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/hospital-discharge): The first 72 hours home carry the highest risk of complications. Answer a few quick questions and we'll build a personalized recovery plan, free, in…
- [Overnight Needs Assessment](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/overnight-care): A couple of quick questions will help identify what kind of overnight coverage fits best - free, in about a minute.
- [Parkinson's Care Planning](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/parkinsons): A few questions about symptoms and mobility will help identify the right level of support - free, in about 2 minutes.
- [Planning Ahead for Care](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/planning-ahead): Families who plan ahead have a much easier time when something does change. A few questions will help you know what signs to watch for.
- [Stroke Recovery Planning](https://mo-care.com/care-paths/stroke-recovery): A few questions about where they are in recovery will help identify the right level of support - free, in about a minute.
- [Senior Outings in Springfield, MO](https://mo-care.com/outings): Senior centers, libraries, parks, museums and events around Springfield, Nixa, Ozark, Republic and Bolivar, and how our caregivers take your loved one there.

- [Eating Well as We Age](https://mo-care.com/guides/eating-well-as-we-age): Appetite and nutritional needs both change with age, and unintended weight loss is one of the most under-recognized warning signs in older adults.

- [Coming Home After a Hospital Stay](https://mo-care.com/guides/hospital-discharge): The first 72 hours home from the hospital carry the highest risk of complications or a return trip to the ER. A little preparation goes a long way.
- [Living Well with Heart Failure](https://mo-care.com/guides/living-well-with-heart-failure): Heart failure means the heart doesn't pump as efficiently as it should - not that it's stopping. With daily monitoring and the right routines, many people…
- [Managing COPD at Home](https://mo-care.com/guides/managing-copd-at-home): COPD makes breathing progressively harder, but pacing, routine, and the right home setup help people stay comfortable and independent longer.
- [Medication Management Made Simple](https://mo-care.com/guides/medication-management): Many older adults manage five or more prescriptions at once. Keeping them straight isn't just about memory - it's one of the most common causes of…
- [Parkinson's Disease at Home](https://mo-care.com/guides/parkinsons-disease-at-home): Parkinson's affects movement, balance, and eventually speech and swallowing. Support looks different at each stage, and fall risk is often the most urgent…
- [Planning for End-of-Life Care](https://mo-care.com/guides/planning-for-end-of-life-care): This is a hard conversation to start, and an even harder one to have too late. Planning ahead, while everyone can still take part, is a gift to the whole…
- [Stroke Recovery at Home](https://mo-care.com/guides/stroke-recovery-at-home): Recovery after a stroke can continue for months, and the type and pace of support usually needs to change along the way.
- [Home Safety Assessment](https://mo-care.com/home-safety-check): Six quick questions, room by room. You'll get a personalized safety checklist at the end, free, about 3 minutes.

## The Dementia Journey (free course) and Family Care Academy

- [The Dementia Journey: A Free Course for Families](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey): A free course for families caring for someone they love. Understand the changes, protect the relationship, and learn how to care without losing yourself.
- [Love Still Lives Here](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/love-still-lives-here): The ending of The Dementia Journey: a free course for families caring for someone they love. The relationship may be changing, but love still lives here.
- [Module 1: You Are Not Failing](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-1): Free dementia course for families. Module 1 sits with the grief, guilt, and love of family caregiving, and teaches a way back after hard moments.
- [Module 2: Understanding the Changes in the Brain](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-2): Free dementia course for families. Module 2: why behaviors are symptoms, why abilities flicker, and when sudden confusion means call the doctor.
- [Module 3: Stop Arguing With Dementia](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-3): Free dementia course for families. Module 3: why facts and corrections backfire, hearing the feeling beneath the words, and the validate-then-redirect sequence.
- [Module 4: When Words and Behaviors Hurt](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-4): Free dementia course for families. Module 4: accusations, anger, and the moments they don't recognize you. The hurt you feel is real, and there are ways through.
- [Module 5: Communication That Creates Calm](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-5): Free dementia course for families. Module 5: approach, pace, choices and dignity, including Teepa Snow's Positive Physical Approach.
- [Module 6: The Stories That Still Exist](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-6): Free dementia course for families. Module 6: identity, music, photographs, and meaningful moments. A person is more than what they can remember today.
- [Module 7: Daily Care Without the Battle](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-7): Free dementia course for families. Module 7: bathing, dressing, meals, and medications with dignity and less conflict, including Teepa Snow's Hand-under-Hand.
- [Module 8: Caregiver Burnout and Accepting Help](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-8): Free dementia course for families. Module 8 is about you: burnout, asking for specific help, the family meeting, and when one pair of hands is no longer enough.
- [Module 9: Hard Decisions, Safety, and What Comes Next](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/module-9): Free dementia course for families. Module 9: driving, living alone, wandering, planning, and the hard conversations, decided by your compass, not ours.
- [What Might This Behavior Be Communicating?](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/behavior-observation): A free printable tool for family caregivers: track what happened before a behavior, what might be underneath it, what helped, and when to call the doctor.
- [Burnout Self-Check & Support Plan](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/burnout-support-plan): A free printable for family caregivers: the burnout warning-sign checklist, your circle of support, crisis numbers, and this week's one ask.
- [The Calm Communication Guide](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/calm-communication-guide): A free printable guide for family caregivers: the calm approach, one-thought rule, the ten-second pause, two choices, the cueing ladder, and the dignity list.
- [Daily Routine & Trigger Tracker](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/daily-routine-tracker): A free printable tracker for family caregivers: each daily task, its best time, what helps, and what makes it harder. The family playbook.
- [Family Caregiver Emotional Check-In](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/emotional-check-in): A free printable check-in for family caregivers: seven gentle questions to ask yourself every week or two.
- [Family Dementia Safety & Emergency Plan](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/safety-emergency-plan): A free printable for families: emergency information, the wandering ready-sheet, and the hospital go-bag checklist, in one plan.
- [100 Story Prompts](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/story-prompts): One hundred invitation-style story prompts for someone living with dementia. Zero interviews, zero quizzes, just doors into the stories that still exist.
- [This Is Who I Am](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/this-is-who-i-am): A one-page life story for someone living with dementia, to share with family, respite workers, hospital staff, and anyone who will ever care for them.
- [What to Say Instead](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/what-to-say-instead): A free printable phrase card for family caregivers: common corrections on the left, kinder responses that actually work on the right.
- [When Dementia Says Something Hurtful](https://mo-care.com/dementia-journey/resources/when-dementia-hurts): A free printable card of grounding statements for family caregivers, for the hour after the words that hurt.

## For professionals

- [Refer a Patient](https://mo-care.com/refer): For discharge planners, social workers and senior-service professionals: refer patients for dependable in-home care across Southwest Missouri, day or night.
- [Referral Partner Portal](https://mo-care.com/referral-partners): We work alongside hospitals, physicians, case managers, and other professionals as an extension of the care team, not just another agency you hand off to.

- [Caregiver in Springfield, MO](https://mo-care.com/jobs/caregiver-springfield): Help older adults stay safe and independent at home. W-2, paid weekly, flexible shifts.
